newsitem.title: USA: AST agrees to change sales practices.
newsitem.headline: AST agrees to change sales practices.

text.p: Computer maker AST Research Inc. agreed to pay $90,000 in government costs and change how it sells lightly used equipment after an investigation by 21 state governments, Florida's attorney general said Thursday.
Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth said the Irvine, Calif.-based company had admitted no wrongdoing and cooperated fully with the probe into how AST resold returned equipment to consumers.
"Computers returned to AST with fewer than 10 hours of use registered on their internal clocks were resold as brand new," Butterworth said in a news release.
The company pledged to sell as new only computers returned in unopened packages, Butterworth said. Used computers sold by AST must be clearly identified as secondhand.
The attorney general's announcement was issued after stock markets closed. AST stock dipped 6.25 cents to $4.75 on Nasdaq.
AST last month hired investment bankers Morgan Stanley to evaluate an offer by Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. to buy all AST stock it does not already own.

In addition to Florida, the 21 states involved in the case were Arizona, California, Arkansas, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Texas, Vermont and West Virginia.
